about: gates/control-audit.js holds a CONTROL-RECORD's total to the cited log's count only where that log ran the record's count set (the gate's L.say lines, plus files a CONTROL-COUNT-INPUT line declares), compared at the record's sha and the log's ref: HEAD sha: exact when equal, 1..count when the log ran more, above the count when the gate grew after the log (a total at it is a STALE TOTAL), HELD TO NO LOG when neither. Graded by gates/pairs/checks/control-audit-holds.sh (node only, no browser, so no phone geometry applies): situation 'fixture arms' is the script's own --selftest arms (8) to (10) in scratch repositories, (10) being the same arms rerun with the hold defanged; situation 'real records' is the audit over this tree's records and newest accepted gatelog - gate 81 COVERED with all six records sound, gate 147 COVERED while its records c8fd052 (assertions changed since) and 34a4a6d (8-hex trial scope) still fault. NOT COVERED: fastgate-drive and records-gate.sh --checks as wholes (run by hand, see the commit), and a full suite.

breaks.name: hold-ignores-the-logs-gated-sha
breaks.why: parseLog no longer reads the log's ref: HEAD line, so every record is held to the newest log's count exactly again - the batch-13 refusal of a grown gate's record, and gate 81's per-build chore

breaks.name: stale-total-accepted
breaks.why: a record over a set the gate grew to after the log is accepted at the log's own count (>= instead of >), so a stale total reads COVERED

breaks.name: count-input-ignored
breaks.why: the CONTROL-COUNT-INPUT declaration is no longer read, so a gate whose count grows with the tree (gate 81) is held to the newest log's count and its older records fault
